final_answer:
SUPPLY AND DEMAND DETERMINE PRICE IN A FREE MARKET THROUGH THE INTERACTION OF BUYERS AND SELLERS. WHEN DEMAND FOR A GOOD OR SERVICE INCREASES, PRICES RISE, ENCOURAGING PRODUCERS TO SUPPLY MORE. CONVERSELY, IF SUPPLY EXCEEDS DEMAND, PRICES FALL TO ENCOURAGE CONSUMPTION. THIS EQUILIBRIUM POINT WHERE SUPPLY MEETS DEMAND SETS THE MARKET PRICE.

WHEN A GOVERNMENT IMPOSES A PRICE CEILING, IT LEGALLY RESTRICTS THE MAXIMUM PRICE SELLERS CAN CHARGE. IF THE CEILING IS SET BELOW THE EQUILIBRIUM PRICE, IT CREATES A SHORTAGE, AS DEMAND EXCEEDS SUPPLY. THIS LEADS TO LONGER WAITING LINES, BLACK MARKETS, AND REDUCED QUALITY OF GOODS OR SERVICES. IF THE CEILING IS ABOVE THE EQUILIBRIUM PRICE, IT HAS NO EFFECT ON THE MARKET.
